goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_', '-')` in `basePath` only replaces the first underscore (non-global), so a hypothetical admin model type name with more than one underscore would not fully normalize to its dasherized `ADMIN_MODELS` entry

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `basePath` changes to `type.replace('_', '-')` to match `ADMIN_MODELS` entries like `'site-customization'` and `'embeddable-host'`. All `ADMIN_MODELS` values shown either have no underscores or correspond to model type names with at most one underscore (e.g., `site_customization` -> `site-customization`, `embeddable_host` -> `embeddable-host`). Therefore, the non-global replace does not introduce a verifiable bug for the actual models handled here; the finding relies on a hypothetical future model name with multiple underscores, which is speculative and not evidenced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb:1 — File named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb now contains `Fabricator(:category)`/`:diff_category`/`:happy_category`/`:private_category`, its content swapped with category_fabricator.rb

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was replaced with a `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the category-related fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, etc.). However, this is primarily a filename/content mismatch/organization issue. Fabrication typically loads all fabricators from `spec/fabricators/**/*.rb`, and the fabricator names (e.g., `:category`) are what matter, not the file name they live in. The diff does not demonstrate a concrete failure (e.g., missing fabricator definitions or missing requires) caused by this swap, so it’s not a verifiable correctness defect from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:10 — update` re-renders the OpenStruct built by `fetch_embedding` without persisting anything; combined with the dead `saveChanges` JS action, the whole singleton "update" route/controller/action chain is vestigial machinery with no live caller and no mutation effect

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` where `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (id: 'default', embeddable_hosts: `EmbeddableHost.all...`). There is no persistence/mutation logic in `update`, and since the model is not an AR record there’s nothing to save anyway. On the client side, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` (empty payload), but `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` does not include any UI element invoking `saveChanges` (only per-host save via `host.save(props)` to `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`). So the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` update chain is effectively a no-op and appears unused within this diff.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Migration builds an INSERT via raw string interpolation of the legacy `embeddable_hosts` site-setting value (`'#{h}'`) with no escaping/parameterization, so a stored value containing a single quote breaks/injects the SQL statement

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` constructs SQL with direct string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Here `h` comes from the legacy `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` (split by newlines) and is not escaped/quoted via connection quoting or parameterization. If any stored host contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), the migration SQL can break or be subject to SQL injection via the stored setting value.
